linkedin.caption:
10 selected citizenship routes: Sao Tome and Principe's USD 90,000 donation, Turkiye's USD 400,000 property and Jordan's JOD 350,000 existing-business test. One main applicant; fees extra, eligibility and approval required.

1. Dominica: USD 200,000 to the Economic Diversification Fund. Antigua and Barbuda: USD 230,000 to the National Development Fund. Both use agent-submitted applications; these are contributions, not property purchases.

2. Grenada: USD 235,000 to the National Transformation Fund. Saint Lucia: USD 240,000 to the National Economic Fund, plus a sworn declaration of at least USD 350,000 in financial resources.

3. Saint Kitts and Nevis: USD 250,000 Sustainable Island State Contribution. Turkiye: USD 400,000 qualifying real estate, with a 3-year resale restriction and a presidential citizenship decision.

4. Sao Tome and Principe: USD 90,000 National Transformation Fund donation. Nauru: USD 115,000 regular Treasury contribution; USD 90,000 offer for applications filed before December 31, 2026. Both add fees.

5. Egypt: USD 250,000 Treasury grant. Jordan, outside Capital Governorate: your eligible asset share must average at least JOD 350,000 over 3 audited years, with 10 Jordanian employees on average and at least 9 each month.

Five roles, identical inputs. Unretouched crops from the real salary calculator, rendered locally. Labels distinguish model estimates from observed salaries. Annual USD model estimates · 2 years; North America · Series A/B · 11-50 staff; Security Auditor; Smart Contract Developer; Product Manager; Technical Writer; Community Manager; Auditor minus Community: USD 70,000/year. Model only; tokens/equity excluded. Screenshot text: $133,000; $101,000; $95,000; $76,000; $63,000

linkedin.caption:
At 2 years, North America, Series A/B and 11-50 staff, the calculator estimates Smart Contract Developer salary at USD 101,000/year. Model output, not observed pay. Tokens and equity are outside this estimate.

1. Security Auditor: USD 133,000/year with the same inputs. The model starts at USD 105,000, multiplies by 1.10 for experience and 1.15 for region, then rounds the result to the nearest USD 1,000.

2. Product Manager: USD 95,000/year in the model at 2 years, North America, Series A/B and 11-50 staff. Its USD 75,000 starting value becomes USD 94,875 before rounding.

3. Technical Writer: USD 76,000/year with those same settings. The model calculates USD 60,000 x 1.10 x 1.15 = USD 75,900 before rounding. Company stage and size each contribute a 1.0 multiplier here.

4. Community Manager: USD 63,000/year at the same 2-year settings. The model's USD 50,000 starting value becomes USD 63,250 before rounding. These five results compare the calculator's assumptions, not employer offers.

5. The model puts Security Auditor at USD 133,000/year and Community Manager at USD 63,000/year: a USD 70,000 gap under identical settings. Reproduce the comparison by changing only Primary Role.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/salary-calculator/li

sourceImages.alt: Career Quiz result for The Builder: Smart Contract Developer, writing on-chain dApp logic. Practice example beside the role card: a local deposit and withdrawal contract with tests.
Career Quiz result for The Strategist: Web3 Product Manager, guiding a decentralized product's vision and roadmap. A wallet-onboarding specification is shown as a practice example.

Career Quiz result for The Analyst: On-Chain Data Analyst, using tools such as Dune to analyze blockchain data. Practice example: a daily active-wallet query with its chain, time window and wallet definition stated.
Career Quiz Community Manager card for The Community Weaver, describing Discord management. Practice example: a support queue recording the issue category, escalation owner and resolution.
Career Quiz Frontend/Web3 Developer card for The Builder: builds dApp interfaces. Practice example: a token-balance screen with disconnected, loading and RPC-error states.

The Builder's three Career Quiz role cards: Smart Contract Developer writes on-chain dApp logic; Frontend/Web3 Developer builds dApp interfaces; Protocol Engineer works on core blockchain infrastructure.

linkedin.caption:
The quiz has four archetypes. The Builder matches with Smart Contract Developer: writing on-chain dApp logic.

Practice example: a local deposit/withdrawal contract with tests.

1. The Strategist matches with Web3 Product Manager: guiding a decentralized product's vision and roadmap.

Practice example: a wallet-onboarding spec with connection, wrong-network and failed-transaction screens.

2. The Analyst matches with On-Chain Data Analyst, using tools such as Dune.

Practice example: a query counting daily active wallets, with the chain, time window and wallet definition stated.

3. The Community Weaver matches with Community Manager, Marketing / Growth Lead and DevRel. The quiz describes Discord management.

Practice example: a support queue with issue category, escalation owner and resolution note.

4. The fifth role match, Frontend/Web3 Developer, shares The Builder archetype with contract development.

Practice example: a token-balance screen with disconnected, loading and RPC-error states.

5. The Builder result recommends Smart Contract Developer, Frontend/Web3 Developer and Protocol Engineer.

threads.title: Five Solidity interview questions with short answers

sourceImages.alt: Solidity interview question SOL-F-04 asks the purpose of view and pure functions. The answer distinguishes an off-chain eth_call, with no network transaction fee, from the same computation inside a transaction, which uses gas. Scope: EVM and Solidity 0.8.x.

Interview question SOL-F-01 compares Solidity data locations. storage persists between calls; memory is writable temporary space for a call; calldata is read-only argument data. Use calldata for reference-type inputs that do not need modification.

Interview question SOL-F-02 with an example modifier: modifier onlyOwner() { require(msg.sender == owner); _; }. The caller check runs before the function body; _; runs the body, then any following code executes. This fragment assumes owner is defined and initialized.

Interview question SOL-F-04 compares view and pure functions. view may read state but cannot modify it; pure may neither read nor modify state. Both execute instructions. Off-chain eth_call has no network transaction fee; execution inside a transaction consumes gas.

Interview question SOL-I-02 on upgradeable proxies and delegatecall. Implementation code uses the proxy's storage and address while preserving msg.sender and msg.value. Upgrades change the implementation pointer; the storage layout must remain compatible.

Interview question SOL-I-03 and storage-packing example. Each box is a 32-byte slot. uint128, uint128, uint256 uses 2 slots; uint128, uint256, uint128 uses 3. Fewer slots do not guarantee cheaper writes; gas depends on access patterns. Do not reorder existing fields in a deployed proxy's storage layout.

linkedin.caption:
A view function can cost gas, and a packed struct can cost more to update.

Five Solidity interview questions with short answers for the EVM and Solidity 0.8.x.

1. Q: How do storage, memory and calldata differ?

A: storage persists between calls. memory is writable scratch space for a call. calldata is read-only argument data. Use calldata for reference-type inputs you do not need to modify.

2. Q: What is a modifier?

A: Reusable logic around a function body. Example: onlyOwner runs require(msg.sender == owner) before _;. The _; placeholder runs the body; code after it runs afterward.

3. Q: What are view and pure for?

A: view may read state but cannot modify it. pure may neither read nor modify state. An off-chain eth_call pays no network fee; execution inside a transaction still consumes gas.

4. Q: How does delegatecall enable upgrades?

A: Implementation code uses the proxy's storage and address, preserving msg.sender and msg.value. Upgrades change the implementation pointer; storage layout must stay compatible.

5. Q: How should you order struct fields for storage packing?

A: Group fields that fit in 32 bytes. uint128, uint128, uint256 uses 2 slots; uint128, uint256, uint128 uses 3. Fewer slots do not guarantee cheaper writes.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/interview-questions/li

Malaysia offers Indian tourists 30 visa-free days; Kazakhstan offers 14 per visit.

Five destinations for ordinary Indian passports, with tourist-entry rules checked October 20, 2026.

1. Malaysia: up to 30 visa-free days for Indian tourists; exemption ends December 31, 2026.

Bring a passport valid 6 months, confirmed return ticket and hotel booking. Submit Malaysia Digital Arrival Card before arrival.

2. Thailand: Indian tourists get 30 visa-free days, 2 entries/calendar year, under September 15, 2026 rules.

Submit TDAC within 3 days before arrival; bring accommodation, onward travel and THB 20,000/person.

3. Kazakhstan: Indian ordinary passports get up to 14 visa-free days per entry, capped at 42 days in any 180-day period.

A 2-week visit fits; leaving and returning does not reset the 42-day allowance.

4. Philippines: 14 visa-free days for Indian tourists, non-extendable and non-convertible.

Bring hotel, funds and onward/return proof; passport valid 6 months beyond the stay. Transit-only trips require a transit visa.

5. Mauritius: Indian passports need no visa. Tourist stays can total up to 6 months/calendar year, subject to border approval.

Bring a return ticket, confirmed stay and funds; passport must outlast the stay.

sourceImages.alt: City photos and directory rankings: 1. Chiang Mai, Thailand, 97/100, estimated USD 900/month; 2. Bangalore, India, 94/100, USD 900; 3. Da Nang, Vietnam, 93/100, USD 850. Each country is represented by its top-rated base. Ties use lower cost, then name. Scores describe cities, not whole countries.

Photos of Chiang Mai, Thailand, and Bangalore, India. Chiang Mai's directory score is 97/100; Bangalore's is 94/100. Both have estimated monthly costs of USD 900, a 3-point score gap at the same budget.

Photos of Da Nang, Vietnam, and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Directory scores and estimated monthly costs: Da Nang 93/100 and USD 850; Kuala Lumpur 90/100 and USD 1,000. Da Nang's budget estimate is USD 150 lower.

Photos of Manila, Philippines, and Siem Reap, Cambodia. Directory scores and estimated monthly costs: Manila 90/100 and USD 1,000; Siem Reap 89/100 and USD 800. Siem Reap ties Phnom Penh's score with an estimated budget USD 50 lower.

Photos of Bali, Indonesia, and Playa del Carmen, Mexico. Both score 88/100 in the directory. Estimated monthly costs: Bali base USD 1,100; Playa del Carmen USD 1,500. The lower-budget tie-break ranks Bali first.

Photos of Madrid, Spain, and Taipei, Taiwan. Directory scores and estimated monthly costs: Madrid 88/100 and USD 2,100; Taipei 87/100 and USD 1,800. Madrid leads Spain's directory cities, ahead of Las Palmas at 86/100.

threads.title: Five frontend dApp interview questions with short answers

sourceImages.alt: Frontend dApp interview question FE-F-02 asks how to display a uint256 token balance. Example for a token with 6 decimals: viem formatUnits(1000000n, 6) returns the string '1'.

Interview question FE-F-01 compares reading and signing. ethers v6: Provider reads chain data; Signer authorizes transactions. viem: Public Client exposes reads; Wallet Client handles signing through a wallet or local account.

Interview question FE-F-02 on token balances. Keep the balance as bigint and use formatUnits(balance, decimals). In viem, formatUnits(1000000n, 6) returns '1'. ERC-20 decimals() is optional; if absent, use verified token metadata or label raw units rather than assuming 18.

Interview question FE-I-01 asks why a transaction is stuck and how the UI should respond. Low fees or an earlier pending nonce can block it. Show pending status. Speed-up uses the same nonce with higher fees; a cancellation is a competing replacement, so the original may confirm first.

Interview question FE-A-01 on displaying a wallet's NFTs across contracts. Query an ownership indexer by wallet and chain, follow pagination, and render token IDs, metadata and images with missing-media fallbacks. A balanceOf call cannot list every collection.

Interview question FE-E-01 compares EIP-712 with personal_sign for off-chain actions. EIP-712 signs typed fields with a domain so wallets can show structured terms. Include chainId and verifyingContract; the application must still check and consume nonces and enforce expiry.

linkedin.caption:
For a 6-decimal token, 1000000 raw units is 1 token. Displaying the raw balance makes a million-fold error.

Five frontend dApp interview questions on reads, units, pending transactions, NFTs and signing.

1. Q: What does a provider do in ethers or viem?

A: In ethers v6, a Provider reads chain data; a Signer authorizes transactions. In viem, Public Client exposes reads and Wallet Client handles signing via a wallet or local account.

2. Q: How do you display a uint256 token balance?

A: Use formatUnits(balance, decimals), keeping balance as bigint. In viem, formatUnits(1000000n, 6) returns '1'. Get decimals for that token and chain; never assume 18.

3. Q: Why is an Ethereum transaction stuck?

A: Low fees or an earlier pending nonce can block it. Show pending status. Speed-up uses the same nonce with higher fees; cancellation competes with the original and can fail.

4. Q: How do you show a wallet's NFTs across contracts?

A: Query an ownership indexer by wallet and chain, paginate results, then render token IDs, metadata and images. Handle missing media. balanceOf cannot list every collection.

5. Q: Why use EIP-712 rather than personal_sign for orders?

A: It signs typed fields with a domain, so wallets can show structured terms. Include chainId and verifyingContract. The app must still enforce nonces and expiry.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/interview-questions/li

threads.title: Five remote-work visas and permits: stay, funds and eligibility

sourceImages.alt: Destination photo beside remote-work visa durations. Japan's Digital Nomad visa allows 6 months with no extension. Thailand's DTV has 5-year multiple-entry validity and allows 180 days per entry. Work, financial, nationality and application-location requirements differ. Rules checked October 20, 2026.

Thailand photo and DTV requirements. Remote-work or freelance evidence and THB 500,000 in funds; 5-year multiple-entry validity, 180 days per entry, with one extension up to 180 days before departure and re-entry. London's checklist requires permanent residence in the UK, Ireland or British Overseas Territories and police clearance issued within 6 months. Apply within London's consular jurisdiction. Checked October 20, 2026.

Malaysia photo and DE Rantau comparison. Minimum annual income: USD 24,000 for tech freelancers or remote employees; USD 60,000 for non-tech talent. Pass lasts 3-12 months, up to 24 with renewal, in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. Employees need a foreign employer; freelancers may serve Malaysian clients. Contracts must have started at least 3 months before application. Checked October 20, 2026.

Japan photo and Digital Nomad visa requirements: at least JPY 10 million annual income; death, injury or illness insurance with at least JPY 10 million for injury or illness treatment. Stay: 6 months, no extension. The principal-applicant nationality list includes the US, but not India; the spouse and child list differs. Checked October 20, 2026.

Costa Rica flag and remote-worker Estancia requirements. Overseas monthly income for the previous year: USD 3,000 individual or USD 4,000 with dependants. Medical cover: at least USD 50,000 for the full stay, including each dependant. Stay: 1 year, renewable once; renewal requires at least 80 days physically in Costa Rica. Checked October 20, 2026.

Barbados flag and Welcome Stamp requirements. Remote work for overseas clients or employers for 12 months; expected income of at least USD 50,000 over that year. Non-refundable fee after approval: USD 2,000 individual or USD 3,000 family. Reapplication is possible after the year. Checked October 20, 2026.

linkedin.caption:
Japan's nomad visa allows 6 months; Thailand's DTV is valid for 5 years, with 180 days per entry.

Compare five remote-work routes. Eligibility depends on your work, finances, nationality and application location.

1. Thailand DTV: 5-year multiple-entry visa; 180 days per entry. Remote workers/freelancers need work evidence and THB 500,000 in funds.

London also requires permanent-residence proof and police clearance.

2. Malaysia's DE Rantau pass: 3-12 months, up to 24 with renewal, for Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan.

Annual income: USD 24,000 for tech freelancers/remote employees; USD 60,000 for non-tech talent.

3. Japan's Digital Nomad visa: 6 months, no extension. Remote workers need JPY 10 million annual income and JPY 10 million medical cover.

The principal-applicant nationality list includes the US; India is not listed.

4. Costa Rica's remote-worker Estancia lasts 1 year, renewable once.

Show USD 3,000/month from overseas work for the previous year (USD 4,000 with dependants), plus USD 50,000 medical cover for the full stay.

5. Barbados Welcome Stamp: 12 months of remote work for overseas clients or employers. Expected income: at least USD 50,000 over that year.

Fee after approval: USD 2,000 individual or USD 3,000 family.

linkedin.caption:
The directory's 5 fastest cities by fixed-broadband download, using a 2026 Q1 snapshot. Monthly budgets are USD estimates.

Check your accommodation's connection separately.

1. 1. Singapore: 576.9 Mbps down / 453.7 up in the 2026 Q1 snapshot, leading the directory on both measures.

Estimated budget: USD 3,000/month, including USD 1,400 rent.

2. 2. Paris, France: 475.9 Mbps down / 346 up in the 2026 Q1 snapshot.

Estimated budget: USD 3,000/month, including USD 1,400 rent. Same budget as Singapore; download is 101 Mbps lower.

3. 3. Shanghai, China: 449.9 Mbps down / 120.3 up in the 2026 Q1 snapshot. Estimated budget: USD 1,800/month.

Third on download, but the lowest upload in this five-city group.

4. 4. Johor, Malaysia: 443.2 Mbps down / 327.9 up in the 2026 Q1 snapshot.

Estimated budget: USD 900/month, including USD 350 rent. That's USD 2,100/month below Singapore's estimate.

5. 5. Santiago, Chile: 429.2 Mbps down / 369.1 up in the 2026 Q1 snapshot.

Estimated budget: USD 1,800/month. Same budget as Shanghai, with upload 248.8 Mbps higher in this snapshot.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/nomads/li

threads.title: Five November Web3 gatherings, with dates and entry conditions

sourceImages.alt: Five event posters with November 2026 dates and cities: Devcon 8, Mumbai, Nov 3-6; Toronto VibeStation, Toronto, Nov 6; W3Node, Cape Town, Nov 12-14; Solana Breakpoint, London, Nov 15-17; CryptoCon Sydney, Sydney, Nov 28-29. Details checked with organizers October 20.

Devcon 8 poster and event details: Mumbai, India, Nov 3-6, 2026. Ethereum talks and workshops on core protocol, privacy and security. Paid general admission has no eligibility test; discounted tickets have separate conditions. Organizer details checked October 20.

Toronto VibeStation poster and event details: Toronto, Canada, Nov 6, 2026. Superteam Canada's Solana coworking day includes project work, lunch and snacks. Free attendance through public applications with host approval; exact address shared with guests. Checked October 20.

W3Node Conference & Hackathon poster and details: Cape Town, South Africa, Nov 12-14, 2026, at Parkview Event Space. Keynotes, technical workshops and a 3-day hackathon. Conference passes are paid; hacker participation is free by application. Checked October 20.

Solana Breakpoint poster and details: London, UK, Nov 15-17, 2026, at Olympia Convention Centre. Topics include stablecoins, tokenized assets and payments. Paid general, developer and student ticket categories. Checked October 20.

CryptoCon Sydney poster and details: ICC Sydney, Australia, Nov 28-29, 2026. Topics include regulation, startups and blockchain infrastructure. General admission covers expo and speaker sessions for free; premium networking and yacht access require paid passes. Checked October 20.

threads.title: Five Caribbean citizenship programs: family prices and asset holding periods

sourceImages.alt: Dominica flag beside a property-holding comparison. Dominica: 3 years from citizenship, or 5 years before resale to another citizenship-by-investment applicant. Saint Kitts and Nevis: approved developer property requires a minimum 7-year hold. Qualifying family and asset conditions differ; fees are extra and approval checks apply.

Dominica flag and two citizenship routes. EDF: USD 200,000 single applicant or USD 250,000 with up to 3 qualifying dependants. Approved property: from USD 200,000 plus USD 75,000 main-applicant government fee. Hold 3 years from citizenship, or 5 before resale to another CBI applicant. Other fees and approval checks apply.

Antigua and Barbuda flag and two citizenship routes. NDF: USD 230,000 for up to 4 qualifying family members plus USD 20,000 processing. Approved property: from USD 300,000, held 5 years from purchase unless replaced with another officially approved property. Larger NDF families retain the USD 230,000 base with incremental processing fees. Other fees and approval checks apply.

Grenada flag and citizenship routes. NTF: USD 235,000 for up to 4 qualifying family members; siblings and parents or grandparents aged 55 or under cost extra. Tourism share: USD 270,000 plus USD 50,000 government contribution; approved units, 2 or more joint buyers and developer equity conditions. Resale to another CBI applicant requires 5 years from citizenship. General approved-project threshold: USD 350,000. Other fees and approval checks apply.

Saint Kitts and Nevis flag and citizenship routes. SISC: USD 250,000 for one applicant or up to 4 qualifying family members. Extra dependants: USD 25,000 under 18 or USD 50,000 at 18+. Approved developer property: from USD 325,000, minimum 7-year hold, plus USD 25,000 main-applicant post-approval fee. Due diligence and purchase costs are extra; approval checks apply.

Saint Lucia flag and citizenship routes. NEF: USD 240,000 for applicant plus up to 3 qualifying dependants. National Action Bonds: USD 300,000 plus USD 50,000 administration, covering any number of qualifying dependants. Bonds stay in the applicant's name for 5 years from first issue and pay no interest. USD 350,000 financial-resources declaration applies. Processing, due diligence and other fees are extra; approval checks apply.

linkedin.caption:
Dominica can require a 3-year property hold; Saint Kitts and Nevis requires 7.

Compare five Caribbean citizenship routes by family contribution and asset rules. USD base amounts exclude fees; approval checks apply.

1. Dominica EDF: USD 200,000 alone or USD 250,000 for applicant + 3 qualifying dependants.

Approved property starts at USD 200,000; hold 3 years from citizenship, or 5 before resale to another CBI applicant.

2. Antigua and Barbuda: USD 230,000 NDF covers a family of up to 4, plus fees.

Approved property starts at USD 300,000, held for 5 years after purchase unless replaced with another officially approved property.

3. Grenada: USD 235,000 NTF for up to 4 people; siblings and parents/grandparents 55 or younger cost extra.

Qualifying tourism shares start at USD 270,000 plus USD 50,000; 5 years before resale to another CBI applicant.

4. Saint Kitts and Nevis: USD 250,000 SISC covers one applicant or family up to 4. Extra dependants: USD 25,000 under 18; USD 50,000 at 18+.

Approved developer property starts at USD 325,000 with a 7-year hold.

5. Saint Lucia: USD 240,000 NEF for applicant + up to 3 qualifying dependants.

Alternative: USD 300,000 National Action Bonds held 5 years without interest, plus USD 50,000 administration; other fees extra.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/citizenship/li

threads.title: Five smart-contract security questions with concrete answers

sourceImages.alt: Smart Contract Auditor interview question AUD-I-02 asks what a signature replay attack is and how to prevent it. The answer explains that a valid signature can be reused: enforce a consumed nonce and the correct signing domain for one-use authorization.

Interview question AUD-F-02 asks what Slither can find. Answer: static analysis for Solidity and Vyper can flag reentrancy, tx.origin authorization and unchecked calls. Findings need review; a clean run does not prove safety.

Interview question AUD-I-01 asks what to check about a staked ERC-20 token. For supported fee-on-transfer tokens, credit balanceAfter minus balanceBefore rather than the requested amount. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection. This pattern assumes compatible token behavior and safe call handling.

Interview question AUD-I-02 on signature replay, with four checks: valid signer, intended domain, unused nonce and unexpired deadline. Bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract and consume the nonce. A deadline limits time; EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.

Interview question AUD-A-02 on fuzzing, with Foundry and Echidna as tools. Example property for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities. Generated inputs or call sequences seek violations. Passing tests is not proof of correctness; results depend on the property, harness, inputs and explored state.

Interview question AUD-E-02 asks how unbounded loops in view functions can cause denial of service. Answer: eth_call uses RPC node resources and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A growing getAllOwners() can fail; bounded pages limit each read.

linkedin.caption:
A valid signature can be reused. A token can transfer less than requested.

Five smart-contract security interview questions on tools, accounting, replay, fuzzing and read-call limits.

1. Q: What is Slither, and what can it find?

A: A Solidity/Vyper static analyzer. It flags reentrancy, tx.origin authorization and unchecked calls. Review each finding; a clean run does not prove safety.

2. Q: What token behavior matters in a staking audit?

A: Transfer fees and rebases. For supported fee-on-transfer tokens, credit the received balance delta. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection.

3. Q: What is signature replay, and how do you stop it?

A: Reusing a valid signed action. Sign and consume a nonce, bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract, and enforce a deadline. EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.

4. Q: What is fuzzing?

A: Generated inputs test properties. Echidna fuzzes call sequences; Foundry supports fuzz and invariant tests. Example for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities.

5. Q: Can an unbounded view loop cause denial of service?

A: Yes. eth_call executes on an RPC node and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A getAllOwners() that grows forever can fail. Return bounded pages instead.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/interview-questions/li

A valid signature can be reused. A token can transfer less than requested.

Five smart-contract security interview questions on tools, accounting, replay, fuzzing and read-call limits.

posts.text:
Q: What is Slither, and what can it find?

A: A Solidity/Vyper static analyzer. It flags reentrancy, tx.origin authorization and unchecked calls. Review each finding; a clean run does not prove safety.
posts.alt: Interview question AUD-F-02 asks what Slither can find. Answer: static analysis for Solidity and Vyper can flag reentrancy, tx.origin authorization and unchecked calls. Findings need review; a clean run does not prove safety.

posts.text:
Q: What token behavior matters in a staking audit?

A: Transfer fees and rebases. For supported fee-on-transfer tokens, credit the received balance delta. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection.
posts.alt: Interview question AUD-I-01 asks what to check about a staked ERC-20 token. For supported fee-on-transfer tokens, credit balanceAfter minus balanceBefore rather than the requested amount. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection. This pattern assumes compatible token behavior and safe call handling.

posts.text:
Q: What is signature replay, and how do you stop it?

A: Reusing a valid signed action. Sign and consume a nonce, bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract, and enforce a deadline. EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.
posts.alt: Interview question AUD-I-02 on signature replay, with four checks: valid signer, intended domain, unused nonce and unexpired deadline. Bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract and consume the nonce. A deadline limits time; EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.

posts.text:
Q: What is fuzzing?

A: Generated inputs test properties. Echidna fuzzes call sequences; Foundry supports fuzz and invariant tests. Example for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities.
posts.alt: Interview question AUD-A-02 on fuzzing, with Foundry and Echidna as tools. Example property for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities. Generated inputs or call sequences seek violations. Passing tests is not proof of correctness; results depend on the property, harness, inputs and explored state.

sourceImages.alt: Destination photo beside tourist-entry rules for US ordinary passports. Japan: 90-day short-stay visa exemption. Thailand: 30 tourist days under the September 15, 2026 scheme. United Kingdom: visa-exempt tourism with an advance ETA unless individually exempt. Checked October 20, 2026.

Japan photo and US ordinary-passport short-stay rules: 90 days under the visa exemption, without income-earning activities. Sightseeing fits this route; paid work requires the appropriate immigration status. Checked October 20, 2026.

Taiwan photo and US ordinary-passport tourist rules. Up to 90 visa-free days, counted from the day after arrival; tourist stay is non-extendable. US passport must cover the stay; carry confirmed return or onward travel and an onward visa if required. Submit Taiwan Arrival Card within 7 days before arrival. Checked October 20, 2026.

Canada photo and entry rules for US citizens: no visitor visa or eTA required. Visits are usually allowed for up to 6 months; the officer may set a different end date. Carry a valid US passport and follow any date on the entry record. Without a stamp, earlier passport expiry can shorten the default stay. Checked October 20, 2026.

UK photo and US tourist-entry rules: visa-free for up to 6 months, with a passport covering the stay, funds and plans to leave. An ETA is normally required before travel: GBP 20 per application, including children. British or Irish citizenship or existing UK permission may create an individual ETA exemption. Checked October 20, 2026.

Thailand photo and US ordinary-passport tourist rules under the September 2026 scheme. Stay: 30 visa-free days, maximum 2 exemption entries per calendar year. Submit free TDAC within 3 days before arrival; show accommodation and onward travel within 30 days. Funds: THB 20,000 per person or THB 40,000 per family. A 30-day extension is discretionary. Checked October 20, 2026.

threads.title: Practice tasks for developers, analysts and community managers

sourceImages.alt: Career Quiz role cards: Smart Contract Developer writes on-chain dApp logic; On-Chain Data Analyst uses tools such as Dune; Community Manager manages Discord. Practice examples alongside the roles: code and tests, a query with methodology, and a support runbook.

Career Quiz card for Smart Contract Developer, with a practice exercise: build a local deposit and withdrawal contract, test unauthorized and repeat withdrawals in Foundry, and include the test command in a README.

Career Quiz card for On-Chain Data Analyst and a practice task: count distinct tx.from addresses per UTC day for one DEX over 30 days. Deliver SQL, chain and contract filters, and a chart. Count repeat swaps once per address per day and label the result transaction senders, not users.

Career Quiz Community Manager card beside a support example. Issue: wallet will not connect. Category: connection. Owner: support moderator. Collect the browser, wallet version and error text, then record the issue in a queue with a handoff note.

The Analyst's Smart Contract Auditor recommendation in the Career Quiz: finds security vulnerabilities in smart contracts. A practice finding format lists the affected function, a failing test and a proposed fix.

The Analyst's three Career Quiz recommendations: On-Chain Data Analyst uses tools such as Dune to analyze blockchain data; Smart Contract Auditor finds contract vulnerabilities; Quantitative Analyst models DeFi protocols' financial risks.

threads.title: Five warm December bases: climate averages and monthly costs

sourceImages.alt: City photos ordered by historical average December rainfall, with temperature averages and monthly USD cost estimates: Lagos 27.6 C, 11 mm, 1,100; Bangkok 27 C, 18 mm, 1,100; Siem Reap 25.3 C, 33 mm, 800; Cartagena 27.5 C, 34 mm, 1,300; Ho Chi Minh City 26.7 C, 64 mm, 1,000.

Lagos, Nigeria, photo and historical December averages: 27.6 C, 11 mm rain and 75% humidity. Estimated monthly cost: USD 1,100. Site safety rating: 4/10; this shortlist uses weather and budget filters.
Bangkok, Thailand, photo and historical December averages: 27 C, 18 mm rain and 62% humidity. Estimated monthly cost: USD 1,100, equal to Lagos; average humidity is 13 percentage points lower.
Siem Reap, Cambodia, photo and historical December averages: 25.3 C, 33 mm rain and 72% humidity. Estimated monthly cost: USD 800, including USD 280 rent.

Cartagena, Colombia, photo and historical December averages: 27.5 C, 34 mm rain and 80% humidity. Estimated monthly cost: USD 1,300. Compared with Siem Reap, average rain is 1 mm higher and monthly cost is USD 500 higher.

Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, photo and historical December averages: 26.7 C, 64 mm rain and 77% humidity. Estimated monthly cost: USD 1,000. Compared with Bangkok, cost is USD 100 lower and average rain is 46 mm higher.

linkedin.caption:
Five December bases with historical monthly averages of at least 25 C and no more than 80 mm rain.

Estimated costs: USD 1,300/month or less. Ordered by average rainfall.

1. Lagos, Nigeria: historical December averages of 27.6 C, 11 mm rain and 75% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,100/month.

Its site safety rating is 4/10, despite meeting the weather and budget filters.

2. Bangkok, Thailand: historical December averages of 27 C, 18 mm rain and 62% humidity.

Estimated cost: USD 1,100/month. Same budget as Lagos, with average humidity 13 percentage points lower.

3. Siem Reap, Cambodia: historical December averages of 25.3 C, 33 mm rain and 72% humidity.

Estimated cost: USD 800/month, including USD 280 rent, the lowest budget in this five-city shortlist.

4. Cartagena, Colombia: historical December averages of 27.5 C, 34 mm rain and 80% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,300/month.

Compared with Siem Reap: 1 mm more average rain and USD 500 more per month.

5. Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: historical December averages of 26.7 C, 64 mm rain and 77% humidity.

Estimated cost: USD 1,000/month, USD 100 below Bangkok with 46 mm more average rain.

instagram.caption:
Five December bases with historical monthly averages of at least 25 C and no more than 80 mm rain.

Estimated costs: USD 1,300/month or less. Ordered by average rainfall.

1. Lagos, Nigeria: historical December averages of 27.6 C, 11 mm rain and 75% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,100/month.

Its site safety rating is 4/10, despite meeting the weather and budget filters.

2. Bangkok, Thailand: historical December averages of 27 C, 18 mm rain and 62% humidity.

Estimated cost: USD 1,100/month. Same budget as Lagos, with average humidity 13 percentage points lower.

3. Siem Reap, Cambodia: historical December averages of 25.3 C, 33 mm rain and 72% humidity.

Estimated cost: USD 800/month, including USD 280 rent, the lowest budget in this five-city shortlist.

4. Cartagena, Colombia: historical December averages of 27.5 C, 34 mm rain and 80% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,300/month.

Compared with Siem Reap: 1 mm more average rain and USD 500 more per month.

5. Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: historical December averages of 26.7 C, 64 mm rain and 77% humidity.

Estimated cost: USD 1,000/month, USD 100 below Bangkok with 46 mm more average rain.

Consensus's date panel names Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre and exhibition dates Feb 2-3. Checked October 20, 2026.

linkedin.caption:
Five announced 2027 Web3 main conferences, in date order: Hong Kong, Cannes, Dubai, Amsterdam and New York.

Dates and venues checked with organizers on Oct 20, 2026.

1. Consensus Hong Kong | Feb 1-3, 2027 | Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre.

Themes: digital assets, AI and the agentic economy. Exhibition: Feb 2-3.

2. EthCC[10] | Apr 12-15, 2027 | Cannes, France.

Palais des Festivals hosts the Ethereum community conference. Full passes cover all 4 days; student and volunteer access options are listed.

3. TOKEN2049 Dubai | Apr 21-22, 2027 | Madinat Jumeirah, Dubai, UAE.

Two-day main crypto conference and exhibition. Ticket checkout offers card or crypto payment.

4. Dutch Blockchain Week Summit | May 19-20, 2027 | Johan Cruijff ArenA, Amsterdam, Netherlands.

Main stage, panels and breakouts. The wider city week runs May 17-23; May 19-20 is the main summit.

5. ETHConf | Jun 14-16, 2027 | Javits Center, New York, US.

ETHGlobal's Ethereum conference covers stablecoins, DeFi and scaling. General passes include stages and expo; Pro adds coworking and the networking lounge.

threads.title: Indian passport: visa-free, visa on arrival and eVisa are different routes

sourceImages.alt: Destination photo and three tourist-entry routes for Indian ordinary passports. Nepal: visa-free. Indonesia: B1 visa on arrival, IDR 500,000 for up to 30 days. Vietnam: advance eVisa, up to 90 days, single or multiple entry. Rules checked October 20, 2026.

Nepal photo and tourist-entry documents for Indian nationals. No visa required. Carry a valid Indian passport or Election Commission voter card; Nepal Tourism Board does not accept Aadhaar as a travel document. Rules checked October 20, 2026.

Bhutan flag and tourist-entry rules for Indian visitors. Entry permit required; carry an Indian passport or voter ID and follow approved permit dates. Adult SDF: INR 1,200 per night. Example: 5 inland nights cost INR 6,000 in SDF, with accommodation and a mandatory guide extra. Checked October 20, 2026.

Maldives flag and tourist-entry checklist for Indian ordinary passports. Visa and admissibility assessed on arrival. Bring an MRZ passport valid at least 1 month, prepaid registered accommodation and return ticket. Each traveller submits the free IMUGA declaration within 96 hours before arrival. Check the stay granted at entry; IMUGA is a declaration, not an eVisa. Checked October 20, 2026.

Indonesia photo and B1 tourist-visa rules for Indian ordinary passports. IDR 500,000 for up to 30 days, with one extension to 60 days total. Passport valid at least 6 months and onward or return ticket required. Online e-VOA must be used within 90 days of issue; that is its use-by period, not the stay length. Checked October 20, 2026.

Vietnam photo and advance eVisa options for Indian tourists. Up to 90 days: USD 25 single-entry or USD 50 multiple-entry, with no refund if refused. A valid passport is required; follow granted dates and use designated eVisa border gates. Checked October 20, 2026.

linkedin.caption:
Indian passport: Nepal is visa-free; Indonesia offers a 30-day visa on arrival; Vietnam offers an advance eVisa.

Five tourist-entry examples with documents, fees and conditions, checked October 20, 2026.

1. Nepal: Indian nationals do not need a visa. Carry a valid Indian passport or Election Commission voter card.

Nepal Tourism Board says Aadhaar is not an accepted travel document.

2. Bhutan: Indian visitors need an entry permit, not a visa. Carry an Indian passport or voter ID.

A 5-night inland trip costs INR 6,000 in adult SDF (INR 1,200/night), plus accommodation and the mandatory guide.

3. Maldives: tourist visa on arrival. Bring an MRZ passport valid at least 1 month, prepaid registered accommodation and return ticket.

Submit the free IMUGA traveller declaration within 96 hours before arrival.

4. Indonesia: Indian passports qualify for B1 visa on arrival, IDR 500,000 for up to 30 days; one extension to 60 days total.

Passport valid at least 6 months and onward/return ticket required. Online e-VOA available.

5. Vietnam: Indian tourists can apply in advance for an eVisa of up to 90 days. USD 25 single-entry or USD 50 multiple-entry; no refund if refused.

Follow the granted dates and use designated eVisa border gates.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/visas/li

threads.title: Five Web3 courses and a lesson from each

sourceImages.alt: Learn Web3 library excerpt with five course and lesson selections. Web3 Fundamentals, 15 lessons: Wallets and Private Keys. Decentralized Finance, 9: Lending and Borrowing in DeFi. Smart Contract Development, 9: Testing Smart Contracts. Web3 Marketing & Community, 8: Growth Metrics and Analytics. AI x Crypto Intersection, 7: Autonomous Agents.

Wallets and Private Keys, lesson 5 of 15 in Web3 Fundamentals. The excerpt contrasts self-custody, where you control keys or account permissions, with custodial services managing them for you. Wallets sign messages and transactions; signatures establish account control, not legal identity.

Lending and Borrowing in DeFi, lesson 2 of 9. Example: $1,000 collateral at 80% loan-to-value gives an $800 borrowing cap. The lesson excerpt explains that allowed LTV depends on the asset, market and risk parameters. Liquidation uses a separate threshold.

Testing Smart Contracts, lesson 5 of 9, with a Foundry test_Transfer code excerpt. The sample transfers 100 raw units from a 1,000-unit balance and asserts 100 received and 900 remaining. Fuzz tests vary the transfer amount to test properties.

Growth Metrics and Analytics, lesson 5 of 8 in Web3 Marketing & Community. The excerpt distinguishes accounts, addresses, transactions, sessions and people. Unique Active Wallets counts addresses over a defined period; one person can control several. Retention measures return activity from a starting cohort.

Autonomous Agents, lesson 2 of 7 in AI x Crypto Intersection. The excerpt separates permission to read a balance, draft a transaction and sign a transfer. Keep model decisions, tools and wallet signing separate; enforce spending caps and contract allowlists.

1. Web3 Fundamentals (15 lessons): Wallets and Private Keys.

Self-custody: you control keys or permissions. A custodian manages them for you. A signature proves account control, not legal identity.

2. Decentralized Finance (9 lessons): Lending and Borrowing in DeFi.

Example: 80% LTV on $1,000 collateral gives an $800 borrowing cap. Liquidation uses a separate threshold, with parameters set per market.

3. Smart Contract Development (9 lessons): Testing Smart Contracts.

The sample transfers 100 units from a 1,000-unit balance and asserts 100 received, 900 left. Foundry fuzz tests vary the amount to test properties.

4. Web3 Marketing & Community (8 lessons): Growth Metrics and Analytics.

Unique Active Wallets counts addresses over a defined period; one person can control several. Retention measures return activity from a starting cohort.

5. AI x Crypto Intersection (7 lessons): Autonomous Agents.

Separate model, tools and wallet. Balance reads should not grant transfer-signing permission. Enforce spending caps and contract allowlists.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/learn/li

threads.title: Five citizenship cost comparisons: contributions, fees and capital

sourceImages.alt: Citizenship directory cards compare costs for one main applicant. Dominica: USD 200,000 EDF contribution plus four fees totaling USD 10,000 gives a USD 210,000 subtotal. Egypt: USD 500,000 deposit capital plus USD 10,000 application fee; capital is repaid in EGP. Unlisted professional, document and transaction costs are extra.

Dominica flag and single-applicant cost table in USD: EDF contribution 200,000; processing 1,000; due diligence 7,500; naturalisation certificate 500; interview 1,000. Subtotal: 210,000. Agent, passport, bank and any enhanced-check costs are extra.
Antigua and Barbuda flag and single-applicant cost table in USD: NDF contribution 230,000; processing 10,000; due diligence 8,500; passport 300. Subtotal: 248,800, with agent charges extra.

Sao Tome and Principe flag and single-applicant cost table in USD: donation 90,000; submission 5,000; citizenship documents 750. Subtotal: 95,750. Documents include registration certificate, passport and national ID. Sponsored applications add 5,000 for benefactor due diligence; agent costs are extra.

Saint Lucia flag and single-applicant bond costs in USD: capital 300,000; administration 50,000; processing 2,000; due diligence 8,000. Subtotal: 360,000. Bonds must be held 5 years and earn no interest; fees are separate from capital. A declaration of at least USD 350,000 in financial resources also applies. Other costs excluded.

Egypt flag and single-applicant cost table: USD 500,000 deposit capital plus USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee, totaling USD 510,000 upfront. The deposit is repaid after 3 years in Egyptian pounds at the Central Bank rate on the repayment date, without interest.

linkedin.caption:
Five citizenship cost comparisons for one main applicant.

Dominica: USD 200,000 fund + 4 fees = USD 210,000. Subtotals exclude unlisted professional, document and transaction costs.

1. Dominica EDF: USD 200,000 + 1,000 processing + 7,500 due diligence + 500 certificate + 1,000 interview = USD 210,000.

Agent, passport, bank and any enhanced-check costs are extra.

2. Antigua and Barbuda NDF, single applicant:
USD 230,000 + 10,000 processing + 8,500 due diligence + 300 passport = USD 248,800.

sourceImages.alt: Invoice Generator sample header: invoice SAMPLE-016 from Sample Freelancer to Sample Client, issued November 16, 2026, due November 30, 2026. The invoice is denominated in USD and marked as a sample, not payable.
Sample invoice row in the Invoice Generator: Documentation draft (hours), quantity 12, rate USD 50, total USD 600. The unit 'hours' appears in Description; there is no separate hours selector.
Two sample invoice rows: Documentation draft, 12 hours at USD 50, totals USD 600. Revision and handoff, 4 hours at USD 50, totals USD 200. Combined subtotal: USD 800.
Sample Invoice Generator totals: USD 800 subtotal, minus USD 50 flat discount, equals USD 750. Tax is set to 0% for this example; the preview omits the zero tax row.

Sample invoice payment notes: USD 750 billed, with example settlement of 750 USDC on Ethereum mainnet at an agreed 1 USD = 1 USDC. Payment Method and Notes are text fields; the tool does not convert currencies. The wallet field is empty and the sample is not payable.

Sample invoice: Sample Freelancer bills Sample Client USD 750 for a documentation project.

#SAMPLE-016, issued November 16, 2026, due November 30. Currency: USD.

Quantity 12 x rate USD 50 = USD 600.

Put 'hours' in Description. The generator has Quantity and Rate fields, with no separate hours selector.

Quantity 4 x rate USD 50 = USD 200. Use Add Item for the second row.

USD 600 draft + USD 200 handoff = USD 800 subtotal.

USD 800 + USD 0 - USD 50 = USD 750.

The discount is USD 50, not 50%. The zero tax rate applies only to this example.

Notes: settle 750 USDC at an agreed 1 USD = 1 USDC. This is an example agreement; the tool does not convert currencies.

5. Sample invoice #SAMPLE-016 totals USD 750, due November 30, 2026. Download PDF exports the invoice and payment notes.

The wallet field is empty; this sample is not payable.
